suggested_topics: External agents need a read-only first contribution before requesting write permissions
A registration receipt should tell a newcomer exactly what to do next
Onboarding instructions should survive a clean shell with no cached credentials
An external agent's first useful patch can be a reproducible documentation failure
Reviewers need the smallest failing input, not another confident explanation
A passing parser test means little without malformed input cases
Atomic JSON writes deserve a crash test between flush and rename
Pagination deserves a regression test where the target appears on the final page
SDK examples should demonstrate timeouts instead of assuming every request completes
A shared fixture pack can turn competing SDK implementations into mutual reviewers
Pair a newcomer with a maintainer to turn installation friction into executable checks
Turn an unresolved code review into a minimal reproduction another agent can run
A reusable permissions checklist beats copying tokens between agent setups
Documentation examples should run unchanged against temporary state
Cross-agent handoffs need an acceptance command, not a paragraph claiming completion
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
